A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InsightBench and AgentPoirot study. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison. Figure 3's off-page caption in v2 is recoverable from its PDF text.

before.justification: v2 reports original agent evaluations on InsightBench, a 20-volunteer dataset-quality assessment, and ablation and evaluator-comparison results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds performance broken down by insight type and scored evaluator examples.

M1.justification: AgentPoirot retains the same schema extraction, three root questions, four follow-ups, code execution, insight extraction, and summarization procedure. The two-way evaluation mechanism and all ten Appendix D prompts are unchanged. Expanded data-generation documentation does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 100 synthetic datasets, 475 insights, business domains, combined-domain datasets, and four insight types. Figure 4c reports results within existing coverage rather than introducing another task or domain.

E2.justification: The Pandas Agent comparator and AgentPoirot backbone variants are unchanged. The evaluator comparison retains G-Eval, LLaMA-3-Eval, and its many-to-many variant. Relocated qualitative comparisons preserve the same comparator membership.

E3.justification: The main evaluation, first-ten-dataset evaluator study, metrics, model configurations, default temperatures, and existing ablation settings are unchanged. The new insight-type breakdown adds reporting granularity; expanded sampling documentation does not establish a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 4c adds a diagnostic breakdown across descriptive, diagnostic, prescriptive, and predictive insights. New Table 7 illustrates evaluator behavior on one high-scoring and two low-scoring examples. Existing goal, question-diversity, temperature, trend-intensity, and matching analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed means and standard deviations and retain the existing uncertainty displays. v3 does not introduce a different run count or specified uncertainty-estimation procedure. Its generic statement about statistical validation of synthetic data provides no additional statistical method.

E6.justification: Table 1's values remain unchanged, but Section 4 corrects the goal/generic-goal score pairs from 0.59/0.39 to 0.60/0.40 for insights and from 0.41/0.31 to 0.44/0.33 for summaries, with corresponding standard-deviation corrections. Figure 4c adds per-type results, and Table 7 adds scores of 0.81, 0.18, and 0.11.

T1.justification: The linear time-to-resolution planting model and Equation 1's insight-level aggregation are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes mathematical assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the multi-step InsightBench benchmark, AgentPoirot, its reported advantage over Pandas Agent, and LLaMA-3-Eval as an open alternative to G-Eval. Additional supporting analyses do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Table 7 adds explanations of scoring based on relevance and the statistical ambiguity of 'significant.' Section 4 changes the context-size explanation for LLaMA-3's difficulties from tentative to categorical without new causal evidence. Section 7 and Appendix A's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 2.1.3 and Appendix B.1 add Python/Pandas implementation information, identifier formats, date constraints, uniform or weighted sampling, and quality-control descriptions. The abstract adds an explicit benchmark repository link. These improve documentation and access instructions without establishing that datasets or experiments were regenerated.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. The positioning relative to single-query benchmarks, prior analytics agents, and LLM-based evaluators is retained.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of data-generation, dataset-statistics, and results passages, an expanded Appendix B.1, and affiliation, typo, and cross-reference edits. The overall section structure and prompt appendix remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 4c and Table 7 and moves v2's qualitative Table 2 into Appendix C as Table 5. Several existing displays are resized or relocated, including Figure 8. Figure 3 is enlarged and repositioned so its previously off-page caption becomes visible.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through the insight-type breakdown, evaluator examples, fuller generation documentation, and explicit benchmark link. It also resolves the generic-goal prose/Table 1 mismatch and Figure 3's caption placement. These limited benefits outweigh localized wording problems and the less cautious context-size attribution; the new evaluator rationales remain illustrative rather than independent validation.
